ready1_open_rewrite.title: SciVerse open question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: In normal individuals, epinephrine initiates a signal transduction pathway by binding to a G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) on the plasma membrane of epithelial lung cells. The GPCR then activates an exchange of a GTP for a GDP on a nearby G protein. This G protein, now activated with the GTP, binds to the GPCR. This allows the release of a G subunit ($G_alpha$) that binds to and activates adenylyl cyclase. Adenylyl cyclase then catalyzes the conversion of ATP to cyclic A ($cAMP$) and $cAMP$ activates a protein kinase (PKA). PKA enables two ATP molecules to bind to the CFTR protein, triggering the opening of a gated channel in the CFTR and allowing for the passive passage of $Cl^-$ out of the cell. The movement of $Cl^-$ into the extracellular fluid creates an electrochemical gradient across the plasma membrane that induces water to move out of the cell. A Na$^+$/K$^+$ pump, also activated by PKA and ATP, helps regulate the electrochemical gradient to maintain an appropriate surface liquid on the epithelial cells. Which molecule initiates the signal transduction pathway described in the passage?
